1301.quote_or_event: “It is so long since this rainbird has had even a glimpse of water.”
1301.explanation: Guru Arjan compares the soul's long longing for the Guru to the rainbird thirsting for rain.
1301.tie_back: The Kural's confidante wants the husband to feel the ache of love for a while; Gurbani gives the same ache of longing, though felt by the devotee rather than inflicted on another.
1301.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 96, Raag Maajh, Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1301._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; next-best only: shares the ache of love-longing, but the Kural is about deliberately making the beloved suffer a little, which has no Sikh parallel. This is spiritual love for God, not romantic love.

1302.quote_or_event: “Sweetness and humility, O Nanak, are the essence of virtue and goodness.”
1302.explanation: Guru Nanak names gentle sweetness and humility as the heart of good conduct.
1302.tie_back: The Kural says a lovers' sulk is good only in small measure, like salt; Gurbani points to the same balance, keeping sweetness rather than letting pride or sourness take over.
1302.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 470, Asa di Vaar, Raag Aasaa, Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1302._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; next-best: matches the spirit of keeping a quarrel from turning sour, but has nothing of the Kural's salt-in-measure image.

1303.quote_or_event: “Humility is the word, forgiveness is the virtue, and sweet speech is the magic mantra.”
1303.explanation: Shaikh Farid teaches that humility, forgiveness and gentle words are what win the Beloved.
1303.tie_back: The Kural says it is cruel not to embrace and reconcile with one who is sulking; Farid's verse gives the forgiving, gentle way that ends such a rift.
1303.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1384, Salok Farid, Bhagat Shaikh Farid (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1303._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; reasonable: both value prompt reconciliation through gentleness, though Farid's lines are general spiritual counsel, not about lovers' sulks.

1304.quote_or_event: “Fareed, answer evil with goodness; do not fill your mind with anger.”
1304.explanation: Shaikh Farid tells the seeker to meet hurt with kindness rather than anger.
1304.tie_back: The Kural warns that failing to soothe a sulking partner is like cutting a wilting creeper at the root; Farid likewise asks us to heal a wounded bond with kindness instead of harshness.
1304.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1381, Salok Farid, Bhagat Shaikh Farid (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1304._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; next-best: shares the call to answer hurt with gentleness, but lacks the Kural's marital setting and creeper image.

1305.quote_or_event: “Wear these three robes, O sister, and you will captivate your Husband Lord.”
1305.explanation: Following his lines on humility, forgiveness and sweet speech, Farid says these virtues are the soul-bride's true garments.
1305.tie_back: The Kural calls a wife's loving pique the ornament of a good husband; Farid names the soul-bride's true ornaments as the virtues that win the Beloved.
1305.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1384, Salok Farid, Bhagat Shaikh Farid (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1305._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; next-best: both speak of what truly adorns a loving relationship, but Farid's adornments are humility and forgiveness rather than pique, so the content differs. This is spiritual love for God, not romantic love.

1306.quote_or_event: “The color of my Lord's Love, however, is permanent, like the dye of the madder plant. So says Ravi Daas, the tanner.”
1306.explanation: Bhagat Ravidas contrasts passing worldly attachments with the deep, fast colour of love for God.
1306.tie_back: The Kural says love without its quarrels is like fruit too ripe or too green; Ravidas also speaks of love in its mature, lasting state, like a dye that does not fade.
1306.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 346, Raag Gauree, Bhagat Ravidas (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1306._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; next-best: both describe love that has properly matured, but Ravidas does not say quarrels are what ripen it. This is spiritual love for God, not romantic love.

1307.quote_or_event: “If I forget my Beloved, even for an instant, suffering overtakes me and peace departs.”
1307.explanation: Guru Nanak says even a moment away from the Beloved's remembrance brings pain.
1307.tie_back: The Kural's lovers feel a pain even inside a quarrel, fearing their time together will be cut short; Guru Nanak likewise treats any moment lost from the Beloved as loss.
1307.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 59, Siree Raag, Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1307._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; reasonable: shares the fear of losing precious time with the beloved, but in Gurbani the loss comes from forgetting God, not from a quarrel. This is spiritual love for God, not romantic love.

1308.quote_or_event: “Without water, she cannot live, even for an instant. God knows the suffering of her mind.”
1308.explanation: Guru Nanak compares the soul to a fish that cannot live without water, and says God knows its inner suffering.
1308.tie_back: The Kural asks what use grieving is when no lover knows it is for him; Gurbani answers that the soul's grief is never unseen, because God knows the pain of the mind.
1308.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 60, Siree Raag, Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1308._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; reasonable: directly addresses whether the beloved knows one's grief, though Gurbani answers yes where the Kural fears no. This is spiritual love for God, not romantic love.

1309.quote_or_event: “Those brides who enjoy their Husband Lord are very blessed, resting in the shade of the mango tree.”
1309.explanation: Guru Nanak pictures the soul-brides united with the Lord as resting at ease in cool shade.
1309.tie_back: The Kural says water is sweet only in the shade, as sulking is sweet only with one who truly loves; Guru Nanak likewise pictures the shade of a secure, mutual love as where sweetness lives.
1309.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 762, Raag Soohee, Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1309._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; next-best: shares the shade image for secure love, but has nothing of sulking. This is spiritual love for God, not romantic love.

1310.quote_or_event: “Even if You cut my body apart, I shall not pull my limbs away from You.”
1310.explanation: Bhagat Kabir declares that no harshness from the Lord will make him draw away.
1310.tie_back: The Kural's heart still wants union with one who lets her sulk wither unsoothed; Kabir's devotion likewise clings to the Beloved whatever the treatment.
1310.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 484, Raag Aasaa, Bhagat Kabir (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1310._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa translation) this session; reasonable: both show love that stays despite neglect; the Kural calls this mere craving, while Kabir praises it as true devotion. This is spiritual love for God, not romantic love.
